If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

#3077. PolyPid: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

PolyPid's regained European rights leave it free to pick a partner before the EMA's late-2027 decision, a choice that will shape its reach.

On its third quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 11, 2026, PolyPid (PYPD +4.60%) announced progress toward its initial commercial launch while expanding its drug pipeline. For long-term investors, the biopharmaceutical company is moving from clinical development to commercial execution with financial backing from partners. Three takeaways from the call stand out for shareholders.

The company is advancing toward its Prescription Drug User Fee Act, or PDUFA, target date of Nov. 28, 2026, for D-PLEX100 to prevent surgical site infections in colorectal procedures. Commercial partner Azurity Pharmaceuticals built out sales channels reaching over 1,700 U.S. hospitals ahead of a planned early 2027 commercial rollout.

Management terminated its European agreement with ADVANZ PHARMA, regaining exclusive regional rights while the European Medicines Agency, or EMA, reviews its Marketing Authorization Application, or MAA. The company's active discussions with potential partners aim to secure European distribution before an expected regulatory decision in late 2027.

The company held $15.5 million in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term deposits on Sept. 30, 2026, excluding a $15 million milestone payment collected from Azurity in October. Existing cash and contract proceeds fund planned operations, including human trials for diabetic foot infections, or DFI, without near-term capital dilution.

Commercial launch preparation is gathering speed through established hospital distribution networks. Azurity brings contracting relationships reaching more than 1,700 target hospitals, positioning the lead product for pharmacy committee evaluations.

Management is also pursuing label expansion into broader abdominal surgeries while advancing pipeline assets into human clinical trials in late 2027.

#3076. GTA VI Is Days Away: Don't Expect GTA V-Style Returns From Take-Two Stock at 5.7 Times Sales

GTA V made Take-Two investors a fortune, but the price of admission this time is very different.

Investors who bought shares of Take-Two Interactive (TTWO +2.97%) after Grand Theft Auto V (GTA V) launched in September 2013 made about 35% in one year, 163% in three, and 673% in five. A $1,000 investment made on the day it was released would have turned into more than $13,000 in 2026.

GTA VI arrives Nov. 19, and CEO Strauss Zelnick says preorders are "tracking far in excess of our initial expectations." The stock bounced after Nov. 9 earnings. But before chasing the bounce, investors should consider what's already priced into the stock's valuation as of Nov. 9.

Management expects fiscal 2027 (ending March 31, 2027) to be "an historic year." It reiterated guidance for net bookings -- the value of games and content sold -- of $8 billion to $8.2 billion, up about 21% from last year.

GTA V has sold nearly 235 million units worldwide over the last 13 years, a testament to the size of the franchise’s audience. This tees up GTA VI to sell into a larger installed base of players, which is contributing to the game's strong preorder trends so far.

When GTA V launched in 2013, Take-Two shares traded at about 1.4 times trailing sales. At the Nov. 9 close, it traded at 5.7 times fiscal 2026 revenue -- more than 4 times higher.

In 2013, investors paid no premium for a game that hadn't yet shown up in sales. Today, they're paying up before GTA VI has even launched.

It seems like too much to ask for the stock to match the returns after GTA V's release in 2013. For the stock to deliver the same returns, Take-Two's market capitalization (share price times shares outstanding) would have to climb from today's $39 billion to $102 billion in three years and $300 billion in five.

Assuming the stock still trades at 5.7 times sales, revenue would need to reach about $17.5 billion in three years and $51.5 billion in five.

But analysts don't expect anything close to those figures. The Wall Street consensus has revenue reaching $9.4 billion by fiscal 2029. At the Nov. 9 close, that's about 4.1 times fiscal 2029 estimates, which isn't cheap.

The biggest risk is that GTA VI is a huge hit but still fails to live up to high expectations in the years following its launch. Take-Two depends on Grand Theft Auto and other hit titles, and a premium valuation leaves little room for disappointment.

To be fair, Take-Two expects over $1 billion in operating cash flow and net cash instead of net debt by the end of the fiscal year. It's on track to report impressive numbers, but valuation matters. That still puts the stock at about 39 times forward cash flow, which implies a lot of growth.

At these valuation levels, I wouldn't buy the post-earnings bounce. With growth already priced in, I would wait until Take-Two reports holiday sales for the December quarter next year. That way, investors can avoid the possibility of a negative surprise that tanks the stock and make an investment decision based on actual post-launch game sales rather than guesswork.

Major indexes remain volatile as investors assess key earnings releases and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Investors with a long-term horizon should look beyond the ongoing noise and focus on stocks that are well-positioned to generate strong returns.

In this regard, recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist stocks with robust growth opportunities. These experts conduct an in-depth analysis of all the macro and micro factors affecting a company, focusing on its long-term growth potential.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

CrowdStrike Holdings is a cloud-native cybersecurity provider. The company recently announced an expanded partnership with Schwarz Digits to bring its Falcon platform to European enterprises.

After hosting several European investor meetings with the CrowdStrike CFO, Stifel analyst Adam Borg reiterated a buy rating on CRWD stock and increased his price target to $230 from $220.

The five-star analyst said that the meetings increased his confidence about CrowdStrike being an "important, well-positioned cybersecurity platform vendor that is an AI beneficiary given its expansive portfolio, unique data set, and ability to both secure AI and use AI to improve security."

Among the key takeaways, Borg noted that AI is driving a major shift in cybersecurity demand as it presents software vulnerabilities that can be exploited by less sophisticated hackers with capabilities that were once limited to government-backed hacking groups. This has led to companies making cybersecurity a top priority, driving customer interest in CrowdStrike's new AI Detection & Response solution and its broader security platform.

Borg added that AI-driven demand is expanding CrowdStrike's pipeline and supporting confidence in the company's higher fiscal 2027 net new annual recurring revenue guidance issued last quarter. Overall, Borg believes that CrowdStrike has multiple growth drivers that can help maintain revenue growth in at least the high-teens and drive improved profitability in the years ahead.

Borg ranks No. 651 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 65% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See CrowdStrike Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Moving on to AST SpaceMobile, a company building a global cellular broadband network in space. Recently, Piper Sandler analyst Alexander Potter initiated coverage of space-related stocks. While the analyst assigned AST SpaceMobile a buy rating with a price target of $100, he has a neutral stance on rocket builders SpaceX and Rocket Lab due to valuation concerns.

"We prefer ASTS, due to a more palatable valuation, and a clearer path to EBITDA upside," said Potter.

The five-star analyst highlighted that AST SpaceMobile builds satellites that connect directly to smartphones, ensuring network connectivity for users everywhere and enabling applications like video calls, streaming, and gaming. Potter added that ASTS' technology helps Mobile Network Operators, or MNOs, expand coverage and offer add-on services to travelers and users in remote locations.

Potter ranks No. 708 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 48% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.2%. See AST SpaceMobile Technical Analysis on TipRanks.

Finally, let's look at Broadcom, a provider of custom AI chips and networking solutions. Recently, Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore reiterated a buy rating on Broadcom stock with a price target of $502.

The five-star analyst is surprised by the underperformance of AVGO stock so far this year compared to its peers, especially given continued momentum in AI-driven demand. Moore cited concerns that competitor MediaTek could gain market share from Broadcom in Google's tensor processing unit chip business and investor preference for faster-growing AI chip names as reasons for the underperformance.

While Moore acknowledged that MediaTek's role in Google's TPU business is growing, he contends that it is unlikely to disrupt Broadcom's position significantly. He expects Broadcom to continue to be the major TPU supplier, with about 80% market share. Overall, Moore believes that concerns about a decline in AVGO's market share to 50% or its eventual replacement seem premature.

"AVGO should retain majority share, sustain strong AI growth, and remain a core compute winner, close behind NVDA," said Moore.

#3073. Evolution Petroleum: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Royalty cash flow needs no drilling spend, so debt paydown and the dividend draw on money the company never has to reinvest.

On its fiscal first quarter of 2027 earnings call, held on Nov. 11, 2026, Evolution Petroleum (EPM -3.64%) announced that growing royalty production in the Permian Basin and Louisiana is generating high-margin cash flow without requiring capital expenditures (capex, or funds spent on drilling and infrastructure). The company is leveraging this zero-capex revenue to pay down debt and protect its long-running quarterly dividend. Three things management said stand out.

Evolution Petroleum is expanding its mineral and royalty portfolio, which lets it collect production revenue while third-party operators cover all drilling and operational costs. This model insulates the company from field-level inflation and capital demands.

Management is monetizing undeveloped land through farm-out deals, transferring drilling rights to partners in exchange for upfront cash and overriding royalty interests (a percentage of revenue with zero expenses). It is applying all cash from these transactions directly toward debt reduction.

With $60 million drawn on its credit facility following a Permian acquisition, the company is prioritizing balance sheet strength over speculative new spending. This capital discipline underpins its 53-quarter track record of returning cash to shareholders.

Production gains across low-cost royalty acreage position the company to expand cash flow as partner operators bring new wells online. Evolution Petroleum holds extensive undeveloped acreage that provides organic upside without burdening the balance sheet. Management is focusing on debt repayment and cost control.

As farm-out transactions yield upfront cash and new royalty wells come online, management maintains a clear capital allocation strategy to protect shareholder value.

#3072. The Homebuying Advice Service Members Need (but Don’t Always Get)

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

VA mortgage borrowers are quietly navigating a knowledge gap. Here’s how to close it.

If your understanding of a VA home loan starts and ends with “it’s for the military,” you’re not alone. For many eligible veterans and service members, the intricate workings (and benefits) of this U.S. government-backed mortgage are obscured behind lackluster guidance.

While there are classes and resources available, the military is broadly wary of steering members in a specific direction, says Alex Rodino, a real estate agent and U.S. Army veteran who served 10 years as an infantry officer and military advisor. “A lot of the course material is just very generic,” he says.

And that’s not a surprise. Considering the sheer size and scope of the military, providing personalized advice on VA loans to all its members would be no easy task.

That leaves real estate agents and lenders as the last line of defense, which is where a big part of the knowledge gap exists. Rodino purchased his first home in 2020 with a VA loan and says he didn’t like how ignorant he felt during the process.

“The reason I actually got my real estate license to begin with was because of that experience I had,” Rodino says. “Looking back on it, I had a lot of questions that didn't really get answered.”

But how can VA borrowers navigate this knowledge gap without having to become mortgage experts in their spare time? Here are some of the most important things to know when considering a VA loan, according to the financial experts and borrowers who have lived it.

“My mortgage broker said, hey, you might qualify for this, look it up,” says Elizabeth Valente, a real estate investor and former U.S. Army officer who bought her first home using a VA loan in 2021. When it came to the application process, she felt crucial information wasn’t readily available to her or fully explained.

In hindsight, Valente says, working with an agent or lender who had detailed VA loan experience would have been beneficial. Not only would it help untangle the specific paperwork and appraisal requirements, but that expertise offers an important layer of support for military borrowers.

“For some processes in the military, it's very hand-holding,” Valente says. “I'll tell you what to wear, what to bring, when to be there.” But that’s not always true when transitioning back to civilian life, and parsing specifics of a loan process can be challenging. “I don't think a typical Realtor would understand what that person's going through,” Valente says.

Finding professionals with the right expertise involves asking questions — and lots of them.

“If I'm the smartest person in the room, we have an issue,” Valente says. “Don't be afraid to tell someone if something doesn't make sense or if you don't understand the numbers.”

Before agreeing to work with a lender or mortgage broker, ask how their process works, what companies they work with, and how familiar they are with VA loans. Treat the initial conversation like an interview — you’re hiring them, not the other way around.

Knowing where to find your Certificate of Eligibility (COE) and how much you might be eligible to borrow is the responsibility of the person applying, Valente says. “All that information — it is available in the [VA] website but you really have to dig for it.”

And this information isn’t recreational reading — your COE lists your "basic entitlement," which is a crucial figure in VA lending. If you have full basic entitlement, the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) generally guarantees 25% of the loan, which in most cases lets you put 0% down.

Why? With a quarter of the loan guaranteed by the VA, the lender is more protected and thus more willing to forgo a down payment.

So how do you know if you have full basic entitlement? Look for the figure $36,000 on your COE. This dollar amount represents full entitlement. Technically, basic entitlement is for loans up to $144,000, but then your bonus entitlement kicks in and you can go higher. The VA doesn’t set loan limits when you have full entitlement — though your lender will still decide how much you can borrow based on your income, debts, credit and the home’s appraised value.

Let’s say you want to buy a home in Fayetteville, North Carolina, and you need a $200,000 loan. In order to put no money down, your entitlement needs to cover at least 25% of the loan amount — in this example, that’s $50,000. After you purchase the home, your COE will show your basic entitlement as $0 and the entitlement charged to a previous loan as $50,000.

“Serving in the military is a unique investing opportunity that most people don't get,” Rodino says. “I wish someone had told me to buy a house when I got to my first duty station.”

If he’d known it was possible or understood how, Rodino says he would have been able to buy in 2017, move in 2020, rent out his first home and then repeat the process. “I'd have three by now and the first one would probably be paid off.”

This particular plan is partly based on the unique schedule of many military members. “Generally, you're moving anywhere from two to four to six years,” Rodino says. Owning multiple properties also leverages two big (and often misunderstood) perks of the VA loan: It’s possible to have more than one active loan at the same time, and after one year, you may be able to convert your primary residence to a rental.

Let’s go back to Fayetteville, North Carolina. After two years, you decide to rent out the home because you’re moving to Bell County, Texas. The home you want to buy in Bell County is $300,000, and in order to make no down payment, you need the VA to guarantee 25% of the loan ($75,000).

Because you no longer have full basic entitlement — remember, you already have an active VA loan elsewhere — your entitlement is capped at 25% of the conforming loan limit in the county where you plan to buy, minus what’s already being used on your first loan ($50,000 in our Fayetteville example).

Now for the math: The current conforming loan limit in Bell County is $832,750. Multiply this figure by 25% and subtract the $50,000 already in use: You have $158,187.50 of entitlement available to you — plenty to guarantee the $75,000 needed on the new loan.

If all of this sounds overwhelming, you’re not wrong. There are resources out there to help you figure all of this out, Rodino says. “The problem is, they're not always practical or they're not always apparent.”

The VA has a website that can walk you through entitlement calculations, but you should also ask your lender, broker or agent. If you’re working with experienced folks, they’ll be able to explain these details and help you get the most out of the VA’s guarantees.

The key takeaway is this: While each VA loan must initially be for a primary residence, borrowers can leverage their entitlement to build an investment portfolio without needing to cough up large down payments.

But these examples don’t consider all of the factors that go into approvals. Like most mortgages, your income, debts and assets dictate your eligibility. And although the VA doesn’t impose credit score minimums, most lenders do — NerdWallet's analysis shows 620 is a common floor.

It’s also important to note that a VA loan’s 0% down isn’t free. VA loans carry a funding fee based on how much you’re putting down and whether it’s your first or subsequent use (certain disabled veterans are exempt). You can pay this up front at closing or roll it into the loan amount; again, your team of professionals should be able to walk you through your options.

“I think there's the assumption that this is what we do: We get our VA home loan and we go buy a home,” says Julie Soares, financial readiness director for the Wounded Warrior Project. When we’re given access to a benefit that offers discounts and perks, it can be hard not to take advantage of it. But this is why financial awareness is critical.

There are a lot of conversations happening right now around homeownership and whether it’s the right choice, especially as affordability remains challenging. So if you haven’t heard it recently, here’s a reminder: Buying property is not the only way to build wealth or create financial security.

“The financial readiness program at Wounded Warrior Project is really leaning into getting further upstream in those conversations,” Soares says. Having a clear understanding of your benefits before you need to use them allows you to make more informed choices.

While it's helpful to understand your entitlement and what you may be eligible to borrow, you don't have to know every little detail about mortgages, or navigate the process alone. Sometimes, the most important thing to know about VA loans is where to turn for help.

If you are unsure of your eligibility or want more information about home loans, you can call the VA's home loans hotline at 877-827-3702.

“Please reach out to Wounded Warrior Project, reach out to the VA, reach out to any service organization,” Soares says. “Not one organization is gonna be able to fix or solve all of these problems. We have to do this as a group.”

#3071. Micron Stock Is Down 40% From Its Peak After the Sell-Off. History Says This Is What Happens Next.

Micron can go on a terrific bull run once again amid favorable conditions in the memory market.

Micron Technology (MU +11.89%) has delivered stellar gains to investors in 2026, but the past few months have been quite forgettable.

Shares of the memory specialist have retreated 40% from the 52-week high reached on June 25. The broader sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, driven by concerns about the sustainability of aggressive infrastructure spending amid rising borrowing costs from high interest rates, has weighed heavily on Micron lately.

However, this isn't the first time that Micron stock has been caught up in a broader market sell-off. Let's see what happened the last time there was a steep sell-off in Micron's shares.

There was a meltdown in technology stocks early last year when President Donald Trump announced tariffs on imports of goods into the U.S. The tariffs created panic among investors, driven by the belief that higher costs of goods due to import taxes were likely to hurt demand for various products.

There were reports that even Micron had to impose a surcharge on some of its products to offset the impact of tariffs. The fear of the tariffs' potential impact on Micron and other semiconductor companies' sales led to a big pullback in tech stocks. The Nasdaq Composite index lost nearly 20% of its value in just two and a half months, between early February and late April last year. Micron stock shed 30% of its value during this period.

However, Micron went on a remarkable bull run following this pullback. Shares of the company have skyrocketed by 830% since the beginning of May 2025 until now. This stunning rally has been fueled by Micron's healthy revenue and earnings growth, driven by a favorable memory market in which demand has significantly outpaced supply.

The good news for Micron investors is that the memory market's dynamics will remain in the company's favor. As such, I won't be surprised to see Micron stock going on another massive rally over the next couple of years, just like what happened after its 2025 sell-off.

Memory demand is poised to outstrip supply for the foreseeable future. Micron's peer SK Hynix (SKHY +9.71%) recently noted that it expects the memory market to remain supply-constrained until 2030. The South Korean memory giant points out that solid demand from AI data centers and emerging applications, such as humanoid robots, will be a tailwind for the market.

Additionally, SK Hynix notes that the new memory factories will take time to come online. As it turns out, more than half of SK Hynix's production capacity for 2027 and 2028 is already booked. Even Samsung estimates it won't be able to meet memory demand until 2028.

It is worth noting that Samsung and SK Hynix control 63% of the global dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) market, according to Counterpoint Research. Meanwhile, they control 47% of the NAND flash market. Micron, on the other hand, has a 24% share of DRAM, while its NAND flash share is 15%. Even Micron management remarked on the previous earnings call that memory and storage supply will tighten in 2027 and 2028.

Not surprisingly, Micron expects fiscal 2027 to be "even better" following a terrific fiscal 2026. Micron's fiscal 2026 ended on Sept. 3, and the company posted a 9x increase in adjusted earnings per share (EPS) to $75.52. The EPS estimates for the next couple of fiscal years point to durable growth in Micron's bottom line.

MU EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

Also, the chart above indicates that analysts have been gradually raising their EPS estimates, which isn't surprising given tight supply conditions. Assuming Micron's EPS jumps to $207.76 in fiscal 2028 and it trades at even 10 times earnings at that time, in line with its current price-to-earnings ratio, the stock could soar to $2,078.

That implies a 172% jump from current levels, suggesting investors can buy a potential multibagger at an attractive valuation following Micron's recent pullback.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, Amarin (AMRN -0.34%) announced its return to profitability following corporate restructuring and reduced operating expenses. The cardiovascular drug maker generated $9 million in operating cash flow through its existing international distribution partnerships across Europe.

Three takeaways from management's comments highlight where the business is headed.

Amarin reduced operating expenses nearly by half after streamlining its business. It generated $9 million in operating cash flow during the quarter, helping deliver $245,000 in net income despite price pressure from U.S. generic competitors.

Four consecutive quarters of positive cash flow and zero debt give Amarin stability as international demand expands. Global partner networks and patent protection through 2039 provide operational advantages as management monitors pricing discipline.

Working with financial advisor Barclays, leadership is evaluating options for capital deployment, including share repurchases.

#3069. First Look: Inside United’s New Club at Washington Dulles

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

The airline’s newest lounge will be the second-largest in the network, offering flyers an upgraded experience at Dulles.

You’ll no longer have to go to the basement to get into a United Club at Washington Dulles International Airport.

The brand-new United Club in the new IAD Concourse E spans nearly 40,000 square feet across an upstairs floor and can seat 630 passengers, making it a significant upgrade to the carrier’s existing lounge portfolio at the airport. It’s the second-largest United Club after its newest lounge in Houston, which opened just weeks earlier.

The new lounge by gates E14 and E16 opens to customers Nov. 10, 2026. United invited me to a media preview of the lounge, and here’s what you can expect inside.

The lounge features several nods to D.C.’s iconic landmarks and monuments, as well as the region’s natural beauty.

When you first enter the lounge, you’ll need to scan your boarding pass and then head up the escalators (stairs and elevators are also available) to get to the lounge.

One of my favorite design features as a former D.C. resident is that escalator ride up, which has been recreated to feel like you’re inside a Metro station.

Thankfully, the escalator ride is not as long as at some stations. Looking at you, Dupont Circle!

Once you're upstairs, you’ll walk into the heart of the lounge, with two buffet stations, a centerpiece bar and plenty of seating options, whether you’re traveling as a group or by yourself. (More on food and beverage options later.)

It’s impossible to miss the soaring ceilings in this lounge, especially compared to the bunker-like atmosphere at some of the existing United Clubs.

Don’t forget to look up, where you’ll see a cherry blossom sculpture, an homage to one of the region’s most popular attractions.

There are also two additional lounging areas on both sides of the central area. One is inspired by the Blue Ridge Mountains, which you can see in the distance.

The other has a cherry blossom theme, with light fixtures that branch out from the ceiling.

Massive windows run throughout the lounge, allowing in tons of natural light and offering fantastic views of the airfield. United has a major presence at IAD, so expect to see plenty of United planes.

The United Club has a full kitchen, allowing it to offer upgraded food options compared to its existing lounges at IAD.

You can expect to find sandwiches, salads and hot protein dishes. The lounge also had a ramen bar and a chili bar set up during my visit.

The two buffet stations are located right next to each other, with a dessert station in between.

If you want something to drink, you can head to the bar or one of the hydration stations throughout the space.

There’s plenty of seating at the bar, which has a double archway design. There are also large TVs if you’re trying to keep up with one of Washington’s many sports teams.

The United Club has eight phone booths for those who need to make a call. They’re split between the two lounging areas in the club.

You'll also find a single-stall private restroom, a wellness room, and dedicated men’s and women’s restrooms.

There are no showers in this lounge. To access a shower in a United lounge, you’ll need to head to the Polaris Lounge, reserved exclusively for eligible business class passengers flying on United and select partner airlines.

You can access the United Club by holding elite status, a lounge membership, the right credit card or an eligible premium cabin ticket.

If there’s availability, United sells day passes at the door for flights departing within three hours. You’ll also need a valid same-day boarding pass on a United or Star Alliance flight.

Holding the right credit card is probably the easiest way to get in. United’s most high-end card comes with a United Club membership, while others might offer one-time passes.

If you’re looking for a United lounge, the newest club in Concourse E is where you want to be. It offers more space, lots of light and elevated food options compared to other United Clubs.

Its massive footprint could also ease overcrowding, a common complaint with other lounges.

One thing to consider is location. The concourses at IAD are spread out, and you may need to take a mobile lounge or train to get there. If you want to check out the lounge, make sure you give yourself enough time to get to your gate.

#3067. American Assets: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Organic property growth accelerated while debt stays locked in at fixed rates through early 2027, creating a potential window for cash flow conversion.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, American Assets (AAT -0.28%) raised its full-year funds from operations, a metric measuring real estate cash flow, guidance to $2.07 per share at the midpoint. The real estate investment trust continues to generate steady income growth across its office, retail, and residential properties despite higher interest rates. Converting signed tenant contracts into cash flow gives the business clear revenue visibility over the next two years. Three things management said stand out.

American Assets raised its full-year earnings outlook after same-store cash net operating income, which tracks property revenue minus operating expenses across existing assets, increased 8.3% during the third quarter. One-time items like property tax refunds boosted the headline rate, but underlying organic property growth still expanded 5.1%.

Demand for move-in ready office suites helped drive office portfolio leasing up to 86%. Expanding this speculative suite program allows American Assets to fill vacant spaces faster than traditional custom builds.

All outstanding company debt remains locked at fixed interest rates or protected through rate swaps through early 2027. Management is preparing for higher borrowing costs when refinancing arrives, but the existing setup protects current cash flows.

High coastal barriers to entry and limited competitive construction keep property demand steady across West Coast markets. Management is watching rental spreads, tenant credit health, and interest rates while converting signed leases into cash flow.

Long-term value depends on disciplined capital allocation and executing on signed lease agreements rather than forcing growth through overpriced acquisitions.

#3062. Prediction Markets Are Arriving in Your Investing App, and That Makes Us Nervous

NerdWallet, Inc. is an independent publisher and comparison service, not an investment advisor. Its articles, interactive tools and other content are provided to you for free, as self-help tools and for informational purposes only. They are not intended to provide investment advice. NerdWallet does not and cannot guarantee the accuracy or applicability of any information in regard to your individual circumstances. Examples are hypothetical, and we encourage you to seek personalized advice from qualified professionals regarding specific investment issues. Our estimates are based on past market performance, and past performance is not a guarantee of future performance.

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. And while our site doesn’t feature every company or financial product available on the market, we’re proud that the guidance we offer, the information we provide and the tools we create are objective, independent, straightforward — and free.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us. This may influence which products we review and write about (and where those products appear on the site), but it in no way affects our recommendations or advice, which are grounded in thousands of hours of research. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews of their products or services. Here is a list of our partners.

Prediction markets are booming, but that doesn’t make them a sound investment strategy.

The investing information provided on this page is for educational purposes only. NerdWallet, Inc. does not offer advisory or brokerage services, nor does it recommend or advise investors to buy or sell particular stocks, securities or other investments.

Around this time every year, we conduct NerdWallet’s annual broker review process. We assess what’s changed in the industry, discuss which brokerage features matter most (and which ones now matter less), and finally, we do the work by opening accounts to test them.

Prediction markets, which have made their way into some of the most popular investing apps, came up more than we expected in testing this year.

At first, we decided to simply collect information on who does and doesn’t offer access to them, without intending to reward or penalize a broker either way. It would be a neutral presentation of facts, not something that would factor into how we scored a broker.

But one afternoon, all together in the office, we confronted an uncomfortable question: “Do prediction markets, and such easy access to them within an investment app, go against NerdWallet’s editorial house views?”

After careful consideration, we all agreed: they do.

So we started to configure our 2027 rubric with a firmer stance against this trendy feature, penalizing brokers that actively market sports and entertainment event contracts, and whose prediction markets come with few, if any, guardrails.

We’ve distilled our discussion down to three main points:

These products are being marketed alongside investments.

We fear they could be discouraging long-term investing.

Let’s start here: Many aspects of trading could be seen as gambling-adjacent. Options, futures, highly leveraged single-day equity bets and even crypto can all easily fall into the “highly speculative” category. So why are we picking on prediction markets in particular?

In our view, a key differentiator is a much lower barrier to entry with few in-app guardrails in place.

Most of the products we mentioned above require some level of fluency — and at times even permission from the broker — to dabble in. To trade options, for example, you need to answer questions about your investing proficiency, your finances and more. And even after approval, the terminology required to trade can be so intimidating that the language itself can become an indirect deterrent.

Event contracts, which form the backbone of prediction markets, are largely presented in the vernacular, and our testing showed approval to trade them is completed with a few taps from the home screen. Moreover, their content is often unrelated to finance — according to a May 2026 report by the Pew Research Center, around 80% of volume on the prediction market platform Kalshi was for sports events[1]Pew Research Center. Trading Volume on Prediction Markets Has Soared in Recent Months. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

Answering a binary question (yes/no; this/that), posed in everyday language about a familiar topic — something like, “Will the Knicks beat the Spurs on Sunday?” — can be far less daunting than figuring out what an options chain is or understanding forex pairs.

In other words, what makes prediction markets accessible to a wider audience is also what makes them problematic, especially when housed within an investing account. Which brings us to our next point.

On the platforms that feature them, we found that prediction markets almost always appear alongside stock and ETF trading. We think this is a mistake. What has made these mobile-first investing apps so good for so long (making it easy to move, manage and invest money through a beautiful interface) is what’s now making us nervous.

For example, most investing platforms let users do any number of smart things with idle cash. They could open an Individual Retirement Account (IRA), a custodial account or a robo-managed portfolio all through a single app. But now, they can dip into that same pot of money to bet on whether Beyoncé or Alicia Keys will play the Super Bowl halftime show.

But is anyone actually trading these event contracts? Let’s use data from publicly traded brokers that offer prediction markets to explore this.

In Q3 2026, Robinhood’s revenue from event contracts rose more than 600% year over year to $173 million, while the number of event contracts traded grew more than sevenfold to 16.4 billion[2]Robinhood. Robinhood Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources . This was the second-highest source of transaction revenue behind options trading. In a forecast reported on by Cointelegraph, Bernstein analysts projected Robinhood’s prediction markets could drive $1.7 billion in annual revenue by 2028[3]Yahoo Finance. Bernstein Sees Robinhood Prediction Markets Reaching $1.7 Billion in Revenue by 2028, Topping Crypto. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

Coinbase's Q1 2026 quarterly report called prediction markets “one of its fastest-scaling products ever, driven by strong retail interest[4]Coinbase. Coinbase Q1 Financial Results Show Resilient Financial Performance Driven by New All-Time High Crypto Trading Volume Market Share. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources ."

In a call discussing Webull’s Q2 results, U.S. CEO Anthony Denier noted trading volume in Webull’s nascent prediction market product grew about 70% quarter over quarter[5]Gloom. Webull (BULL) Q2 2026 earnings call transcript. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources .

Gemini’s Q2 report shows prediction market volume rose 93% quarter over quarter[6]Gemini. Shareholder Update Q2 2026. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

So, now that we’ve established that these markets are growing in popularity — and investing platforms appear to have a large incentive to lean into them — how are all those event contract traders faring? That brings us to our final point.

Is all this even worth it? Several studies show how hard it is to actually turn a profit in prediction markets. Here are a few:

One study, conducted by researchers at ESSEC Business School, HEC Montréal and the University of Toronto's Rotman School of Management, covered 2.4 million Polymarket accounts across $67 billion in trading volume between November 2022 and March 2026, and found that 69% of users lost money[7]SSRN. Who Wins and Who Loses In Prediction Markets? Evidence from Polymarket. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources . Moreover, the top 1% of users who made a profit accounted for about 76% of all gains. Translation: Even if you did turn a profit, there’s a good chance you didn’t make much.

A Bloomberg analysis supports this: From January 2025 to April 2026, more than 100,000 Polymarket accounts lost at least $1,000[8]Bloomberg. Most Prediction Market Traders Are Losing Money While Bots Rack Up Gains. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources . Of the 2 million active wallets studied, almost half made or lost less than $10 during the period, while far fewer accounts collected larger profits.

A separate Wall Street Journal analysis echoed the same trend: 67% of Polymarket profits go to 0.1% of accounts, and more than 70% of Polymarket users lost money[9]The Wall Street Journal. Why Almost Everyone Loses—Except a Few Sharks—on Prediction Markets. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources .

While there is far less data available on Kalshi trades (Polymarket runs on a public blockchain, making it easy to extract and analyze data), a Kalshi spokesperson confirmed in the Wall Street Journal analysis above that one month of data in 2026 showed there were 2.9 unprofitable users to each profitable user[10]Wall Street Journal. Why Almost Everyone Loses—Except a Few Sharks—on Prediction Markets. Accessed Nov 10, 2026. View all sources .

The first study above discusses how event contract trading is binary and zero-sum: If one trader wins, another loses. This means traders allocating money to these instruments could be missing out on aspects of equity markets that have helped create long-term wealth for previous generations.

“Unlike equity markets, there is no equity premium, no dividends, and no passive investment options. Their short maturities naturally encourage short-horizon trading, which is precisely what the behavioral finance literature has suggested is most destructive to wealth accumulation. Given the rapid growth of these platforms and their role as a potential entry point for young investors, understanding who bears the losses has direct implications for investor welfare and market regulation.”

As a reminder, the vast majority of Polymarket users bore the losses.

At NerdWallet, our mission has always been to help people make smarter financial decisions, so we’re sticking by that. Starting with our 2027 ratings, brokers that offer easy access to sports and entertainment event contracts will lose points in our scoring system because we believe this new product has the potential to harm long-term wealth building and doesn’t belong in investing platforms.

So, what’s a better way forward? Bring back the friction and make prediction markets a separate app. Financial institutions, businesses and individuals can still explore legitimate use cases for prediction markets, such as forecasting and hedging. And we’re not here to stop anyone from trading event contracts for entertainment with extra money. We just don’t want these markets so easily conflated with the legitimate investing vehicles these apps already offer. And our reviews will reflect that.

#3059. Which Gold ETF Is the Better Buy: iShares’ Gold Trust IAU or Sprott’s Gold Miners SGDM?

Mining stocks have led recently, but they have also fallen much harder than bullion. Cost and volatility differences reveal which fund fits your goals.

Sprott Gold Miners ETF (SGDM -2.12%) targets the equity performance of gold-producing companies, whereas iShares Gold Trust (IAU -1.15%) tracks the spot price movements of physical gold bullion.

These two funds serve the gold market through entirely different mechanisms. One relies on the operational efficiency and profitability of mining firms, while the other fluctuates purely with the spot price of the metal. This distinction makes them useful for different strategies, whether seeking a cleaner hedge against inflation or participating in the business side of extraction.

Beta measures price volatility relative to the S&P 500; beta is calculated from monthly returns over the available fund history (up to five years). The 1-yr return represents total return over the trailing 12 months. Dividend yield is the trailing-12-month distribution yield.

iShares Gold Trust is notably more affordable, with an expense ratio of 0.25% compared to 0.46% for Sprott Gold Miners ETF. This lower cost could make it more attractive for long-term commodity exposure.

iShares Gold Trust provides direct exposure to the commodity markets by tracking the daily spot price performance of gold bullion. It is categorized as Cash & Others at 100%, and its portfolio consists entirely of Physical Gold at 100%. Managed by iShares Delaware Trust Sponsor, it offers a way for investors to gain exposure to the precious metal without the logistical burden of holding physical bars and was launched in 2005.

Sprott Gold Miners ETF targets gold-producing companies in the U.S. and Canada, primarily those trading on major exchanges. It focuses on Basic Materials at 100%, and its largest positions include Agnico Eagle Mines at 10.04%, Newmont (NEM -1.24%) at 7.84%, and Barrick Mining at 7.38%. The fund usually invests 90% of its net assets in its underlying index and was launched in 2014.

For more guidance on ETF investing, check out the full guide at this link.

Gold peaked in January after a historic run, then pulled back sharply as interest rates and Treasury yields stayed high. Gold pays no interest, so higher yields make it less appealing next to bonds. Even so, long-term investors hold it as a hedge when stocks or the dollar wobble, and central banks and ETF buyers around the world have kept adding.

For long-term investors, the iShares Gold Trust (IAU) looks like the better way to own it. It holds physical gold, charges roughly half what Sprott's miners fund does, and is one of the largest gold funds around.

SGDM owns 43 gold miners, and when gold jumps, miners can jump more. That is why it has beaten gold at times and pays a small dividend. Miners also carry rising costs, and gold stocks have pulled back too. IAU pays no dividend, but it tracks gold without the bumpier ride.

Even after the pullback, IAU offers a simple, low-cost way to hold gold for the long haul without betting on mine managers or costs. SGDM works best as a small add-on for investors seeking additional gold risk.

#3051. Why Gevo Stock Rocketed Higher Today

Breaking company records has a funny way of motivating the bulls.

Outpacing the 1.3% rise in the S&P 500, shares of Gevo (GEVO +30.94%) soared today following the company's reporting of third-quarter 2026 financial results after the market closed yesterday. Between that and an analyst taking a more auspicious stance on the specialty chemicals stock, bulls had plenty of fodder to feast upon.

Gevo shares closed at $1.82 today, up 30.9% from Tuesday's close of $1.39.

Posting Q3 2026 sales of $83 million, Gevo exceeded analysts' expectations of $54.5 million. The company's Q3 2026 sales, driven by the strength of its carbon business, represented a new high-water mark. At the bottom of the income statement, Gevo provided another surprise, reporting adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.12 -- better than the $0.02 analysts had anticipated.

In Q3 2026, Gevo also reported company records for adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and cash from operations: $44 million and $41 million, respectively.

Heralding the company's strong performance, Gevo's chief executive officer Paul Boom stated: "We said we would build a carbon business that stands on its own in 2026. These results show it's working."

Gevo also raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA forecast to $90 million from $60 million.

In addition to developing technology to produce various renewable products, including motor fuels and chemicals, Gevo owns and operates an ethanol plant with an adjacent carbon capture and storage facility.

Trading at 1.5 times trailing sales, Gevo stock is available at a discount to its five-year average P/S ratio of 8.3. Prospective investors should recognize, however, that the company doesn't have a long track record of generating profits, so the stock is best suited for those comfortable with more aggressive investment. Conservative investors, on the other hand, have plenty of other options for chemical stocks.

#3048. Top Wall Street analysts like these 3 stocks for their solid growth potential

Investors are closely monitoring earnings releases of artificial intelligence companies amid concerns about the durability of high spending and demand. While quarterly results provide key insights into a company's performance and execution, it is prudent to focus on long-term prospects and look beyond short-term fluctuations.

Top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick stocks with attractive long-term prospects as their assessments are backed by in-depth research of a company's fundamentals and growth opportunities.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

AI-powered data analytics provider Palantir Technologies is this week's first pick. The company reported market-beating second-quarter results. Moreover, Palantir raised its full-year guidance and now expects U.S. commercial business revenue to grow by at least 134%.

Following the Q2 print, Bank of America analyst Mariana Perez Mora reiterated a buy rating on PLTR stock with a price target of $255. Mora said that Palantir's performance reflects the success of its AI strategy, which focuses on delivering the right infrastructure to customers and ensuring better outcomes.

"The main driver continues to be the U.S. commercial business, which now represents almost 40% of total (vs. 30% a year ago and just 20% a couple of years back)," noted Mora.

The five-star analyst highlighted the 149% growth in Palantir's U.S. commercial business in Q2 2026 and the expansion in its customer base and engagement levels, with clients pursuing more integrated relationships. Mora noted that the U.S. commercial customer count increased 35% year-over-year to 653, with trailing twelve months revenue per customer surging 76% to $3.5 million in the second quarter.

Citing strength across Palantir's commercial and government segments, Mora increased her sales and earnings per share estimates for 2026-2028. The analyst attributed the increase in her estimates to the growth in the commercial business, backed by stronger total contract value in the second quarter.

Mora ranks No. 444 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 32.6%. See Palantir Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

E-commerce and cloud computing giant Amazon impressed investors with its strong second-quarter results. Revenue from the company's Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud business surged 37%, marking the unit's fastest growth since 2021.

In reaction to the Q2 2026 performance, JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth reiterated a buy rating on Amazon stock and raised his price target to $365 from $330, saying that it remains the firm's Best Idea. Anmuth highlighted that the company's forex-neutral top-line growth accelerated to 20% in Q2 2026, the fastest in 20 quarters. He added that the top line gained from acceleration across both AWS and stores.

The five-star analyst noted that AWS growth of 37% was the fastest in 18 quarters, with backlog jumping nearly 2.5x year-over-year and 36% sequentially to $496 billion. Amazon's backlog gained from robust demand across both core workloads and AI adoption. Anmuth also observed the strength in AWS' AI and chips businesses, Graviton revenue commitments, and AWS' core business.

Notably, Anmuth believes that the core AWS business is highly correlated to AI revenue, and he expects further strengthening of this relationship as more AI workloads move into full-scale production and fuel higher demand. Overall, the analyst is more optimistic on Amazon following Q2 results and raised his 2026 and 2027 sales estimates by about 1% to 2% and operating income by about 5% to 7%.

"Importantly, management emphasized that the [return on invested capital] on its AI investments is compelling and it has a clear line-of-sight to strong financial returns," said Anmuth.

Anmuth ranks No. 717 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.5%. See Amazon Statistics on TipRanks.

Moving on to Lam Research, a supplier of semiconductor manufacturing equipment and services. Thanks to AI-driven demand, the company delivered better-than-anticipated fiscal fourth quarter results.

In reaction to the solid results, Oppenheimer analyst Edward Yang reaffirmed a buy rating on LRCX stock with a price target of $400. Yang stated that Lam Research exceeded June-quarter expectations despite the high bar, driven by strong performance of the Customer Support Business Group and doubling of NAND revenue from the prior quarter. He also cited the improvement in Q4 FY26 gross margin.

The five-star analyst highlighted that Lam Research's September-quarter revenue and EPS outlook exceeded the Street's expectations by mid-teens percentages. Yang added that the company increased its wafer fabrication equipment spending outlook to the low-$150 billion range, up from its prior $140 billion estimate.

Importantly, Yang noted that Lam Research called calendar year 2027 "extraordinary," citing persistent supply shortages and the addition of 8 to 10 new fabrication plants. The analyst raised his 2027 revenue and EPS estimates by 7% and 9% to $33 billion and $8.88, respectively. Yang also increased his 2028 revenue and EPS estimates by 7% and 8% to $36.6 billion and $9.89, respectively.

"It's the cleanest way to play AI-driven 3D scaling across memory, foundry/logic, and packaging," said Yang about LRCX.

TL;DR: Rates fell today, but not by enough to change your mortgage math.

Mortgage rates are a little lower today. It probably won't last, thanks to new inflation data that has investors even more confident that the Federal Reserve will hike rates next month. You can read more on that below the charts.

Today, the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked down to 6.9% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is eight basis points lower than yesterday and 17 basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

This morning the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) dropped the October Consumer Price Index, which shows that inflation rose another 0.4% last month. This outpaced expectations: Economists had forecasted an increase of 0.3%. CPI is one of two key measures of inflation, which the Federal Reserve aims to keep in check relative to the strength of the labor market. (The Fed looks more closely at a different inflation measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures Index, which comes out Nov. 25.)

Raising the federal funds rate is the Fed’s main tool for bringing inflation down, and futures traders are banking on a rate hike when the committee meets Dec. 8-9. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates directly, but an anticipated rate hike can put upward pressure on mortgage rates, which respond to investors’ expectations for the economy and Fed policy.

Central bankers raised the federal funds rate in September, but it hasn’t been enough to pull inflation closer to the Fed’s target of 2%. Investors aren’t sure that one more hike in December will do the trick, either. According to CME FedWatch, further rate hikes may be in store for January.

» MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.4% or higher.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

Wall Street rallied on Wednesday, November 11, as renewed optimism surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) fueled a broad recovery in technology stocks following Tuesday's inflation-driven sell-off. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +1.60%) led major indexes higher, climbing 1.60% to 25,466, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC +1.31%) gained 1.29% to 7,618. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +0.49%) advanced a more modest 0.49% to 52,486.

Gold prices declined 0.98% to $3,990.70, reflecting a shift in investor appetite toward equities. Utilities led sector gains, followed by strength in technology, while consumer cyclical stocks lagged.

CoreWeave (CRWV +24.71%) shares surged 24.71% after reporting record quarterly results and raising its revenue outlook, while Micron Technology (MU +11.89%) gained 11.89% as semiconductor names recovered from earlier weekly losses. Oracle (ORCL +8.81%) advanced 8.83% following news of record energy-saving milestones for its utility customers, and Apple (AAPL +2.04%) rose 2.04% to reach a fresh record high during the session.

Wednesday's rally offered an encouraging sign for investors following Tuesday's inflation-driven sell-off, but the underlying economic concerns haven't disappeared. CoreWeave's strong earnings and improved revenue outlook helped reinforce confidence in AI infrastructure spending, suggesting that demand for computing capacity remains robust despite concerns about elevated valuations and the substantial cost of expansion.

However, the recovery was particularly strong among technology and semiconductor stocks, leaving questions about the breadth and sustainability of the rally. Continued gains will likely depend on whether corporate earnings can justify elevated valuations, particularly as higher interest rates increase financing costs and reduce the appeal of future earnings relative to fixed-income investments.

Looking ahead, investors should watch whether the S&P 500 can sustain its recovery as bond trading resumes following Veterans Day. With the 10-year Treasury yield approaching 5% before the holiday, renewed upward pressure on yields could challenge the rally. Upcoming earnings from Nvidia will also provide an important test of AI demand heading into 2027. A sustained year-end advance will likely require both resilient corporate earnings and greater confidence in the Federal Reserve's interest rate outlook.

#3040. Five Below vs. GameStop: Which Retailer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Five Below's rapid store expansion goes head-to-head with GameStop's cash-rich pivot, and the valuation gap may be wider than it first appears.

Can a discount retailer's aggressive expansion strategy beat a legacy gaming brand's financial pivot? Investors comparing Five Below (FIVE -1.09%) and GameStop (GME +0.47%) face a choice between rapid physical growth and deep value.

Five Below focuses on high-volume, low-cost variety goods for younger shoppers, while GameStop relies on its loyal gaming community and immense cash reserves. Both companies navigate a shifting retail environment, but their strategies for generating shareholder value through 2027 differ significantly in execution, risk, and capital allocation.

Five Below operates as a specialty retailer focused on trend-right, extreme-value products, typically priced between one and five dollars. In its latest annual report, the company notes that it targets an economically influential demographic of kids, pre-teens, and teens, alongside value-oriented shoppers. This niche positioning within retail stocks allows the business to maintain a broad vendor base of approximately 1,000 suppliers while operating 2,022 stores.

In FY 2025, revenue reached about $4.8 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 22.9% compared to the previous year. This substantial increase in sales helped the company generate a net income of roughly $358.6 million. The net margin for the period is close to 7.5%, showcasing the company's ability to maintain profitability while aggressively scaling its store count across the United States.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.9x. This metric, which compares total debt to the value of shareholder equity, suggests a balanced capital structure for the retailer. The current ratio, a measure of a company's ability to pay short-term obligations with short-term assets, is roughly 2.0x, while free cash flow for the year reached around $411.7 million.

GameStop, according to its latest annual report, operates a global network of stores and e-commerce platforms specializing in video games, collectibles, and entertainment products. The company maintains critical relationships with major gaming vendors including Nintendo (NTDOF -1.16%), Sony (SONY -0.82%), and Microsoft Corp. (MSFT -2.26%), which provide the majority of its new product inventory. Through its loyalty programs, the retailer fosters a dedicated community of members who receive exclusive rewards.

In FY 2025, revenue reached around $3.6 billion, which was a decrease of approximately 5.1% compared to the prior period. Despite the decline in top-line sales, the company reported a net income of roughly $418.4 million. This resulted in a net margin of approximately 11.5%, a significant improvement in profitability that suggests more efficient management of its global retail operations.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.8x. The company maintains an exceptionally high current ratio of approximately 15.3x, indicating a massive surplus of liquid assets relative to its short-term liabilities. Free cash flow for the year reached around $597.3 million, supporting the company's efforts to transform its business model and invest in new opportunities.

Five Below faces intense competition from physical and online retailers, including big box stores like Walmart Inc.(WMT +0.10%) and Target Corp. (TGT +0.57%), as well as Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN -1.74%). The company is also navigating legal and litigation risks, including federal class action lawsuits related to its inventory management and growth projections. Furthermore, its reliance on foreign manufacturing, primarily in China, exposes the business to supply chain disruptions and shifting trade policies regarding tariffs.

GameStop operates in a highly competitive environment where a rapid industry shift toward digital, download-only gaming threatens its traditional physical media sales. The company also deals with strategic risks involving its investments in Bitcoin, which can introduce significant volatility to its financial results. Additionally, its reliance on a single distribution facility in Texas and significant outstanding convertible notes could limit its future financial flexibility.

GameStop appears more attractively valued based on its Forward P/E, though Five Below trades at a more modest P/S ratio relative to its sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

GameStop has benefited greatly from its recent move to emphasize trading cards and collectibles alongside its video game business, and it is paying off. It caught many investors' eyes when it made an unsolicited bid to buy eBay Inc. (EBAY -0.68%) earlier this year, too. Though that was rejected, reports say the CEO, Ryan Cohen, is still pursuing options around eBay, including striking a partnership with the business. Cohen has shown a lot of faith in his ability to boost GameStop's business. He's been a heavy buyer of company shares of late.

In its most recent quarter, net sales were $790.2 million, compared to $972.2 million in the prior year's second quarter. The decrease primarily reflects the prior-year launch of Nintendo Switch 2, planned store closures, and the divestiture of the company's France operations.

There were big positives, though: collectibles net sales were $356.3 million for the second quarter, or 45% of net sales, compared to $227.6 million, or about 23% of net sales, in the prior year's second quarter. Its pivot appears to have momentum.

Meanwhile, Five Below is one of the hottest names in brick-and-mortar retail. The company sees impressive unit economics, with each new store it opens paying back its cost in about a year, which has management focused on growing through opening more stores. The plan is to add 150 stores annually, and Wall Street analysts say that even at that pace, management appears to have a good focus on finding quality locations.

The company has really taken to social media as a driver of foot traffic, leading to a very impressive 18% increase in same-store sales in the first half of its current fiscal year 2027. Just as impressive, the company continues to expand its gross margins even as the Trump tariffs have raised costs for much of the product it sells.

For fiscal 2027, analysts see revenue growing 20% to $5.17 billion, with net income jumping 40% or more to around $360 million.

GameStop shares have been a fun ride at times. But Five Below has the profile of a once-in-a-decade retailer that promises to continue to grow well for years to come. Even though it comes at a premium based on its P/E ratio, Five Below is the choice for long-term investors.

#3037. Chefs' Warehouse: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Margin expansion from direct sourcing and AI pricing tools may offset fuel cost pressures, a key test of durable profitability.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, Chefs' Warehouse (CHEF -0.81%) raised its full-year financial guidance after generating $1.14 billion in quarterly net sales. The specialty food distributor expanded gross profit margins through direct purchasing scale and AI pricing technology. Maintaining momentum across premier dining customers while managing fuel costs positions the business for durable compounding.

Chefs' Warehouse expanded organic net sales by 10.3% during the third quarter of 2026, supported by a 7.2% rise in unique item placements and a 4.4% increase in unique customers. Customer demand remained steady across regional markets as sales teams expanded product categories and added premier restaurant accounts.

During the third quarter, management issued a new $75 million seven-year term loan to settle its 2028 convertible notes. The transaction addresses near-term debt maturities, reduces the fully diluted share count to roughly 43.0 million shares, and keeps net debt leverage at 1.4 times adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (adjusted EBITDA), well within the company's target range of 1.5 to 2.5 times.

Gross profit rose 15% to $284 million as gross profit margin reached 25%, an 84 basis point improvement over the prior year quarter. Expanding distribution facilities lets the business buy products directly from suppliers in larger volumes and eliminate less-than-truckload (LTL) shipping, which means shipping partial loads at higher unit freight costs.

Higher diesel fuel expenses continue to press on operating costs, but rising gross profit margins from pricing discipline and digital tools are offsetting the pressure. Management is expanding distribution capacity in Texas, New England, and Las Vegas while integrating artificial intelligence across sales routes to manage elevated inflation.

Long-term target execution remains on track as distribution scale expands across core metropolitan regions. The leadership team expects high-margin customer demand to sustain profitability into 2027.
